bull.b: Deucrictibant has demonstrated substantial and sustained reductions in HAE attacks across pivotal and extension studies. Durable efficacy across treatment settings strengthens the potential product profile, supports differentiation in a rare-disease market, and could underpin adoption if regulatory approvals are obtained.

Extremely low debt reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves flexibility while Pharvaris funds clinical development and prepares for commercialization. The sizable equity base provides a stronger financial foundation than a highly leveraged biotechnology company facing lengthy development timelines.

A single oral therapy platform addressing both acute HAE attacks and prevention could broaden Pharvaris’s commercial opportunity and simplify its strategic focus. Coverage of multiple treatment needs may support a unified franchise and improve the potential value of successful commercialization.

bear.b: Pharvaris has not yet generated product revenue, while losses remain very large and materially higher than in earlier years. Until a candidate is approved and commercialized, the company lacks operating earnings to offset development costs, leaving financial performance dependent on future execution.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow indicates that Pharvaris continues to consume substantial funds to support operations and development. This burn can reduce financial flexibility over time and may require additional funding before commercial products generate meaningful cash inflows.

The business remains dependent on successful regulatory outcomes and the transition from clinical development to commercialization. Reviews are still underway and the prophylaxis filing is prospective, so delays or unsuccessful execution could defer revenue generation and extend the period of heavy investment.
